statement: Editorial citation key for earlier context excerpts; no mathematical assertion by the manuscript author.

statement: Does the proposed finite-type category of schematic objects over a noetherian base have the listed finite-limit, quotient and descent properties?
reconstruction: Pro reads pro-schématique; K91-08 reads quasi-schématique. Neither identification with a topos nor a definition of the exact category is supplied here.
check_reason: The question is real, but the category word is disputed between transcriptions. Retain the question; do not silently identify it with the category of schemes or a Grothendieck topos.

statement: The sheet asks whether the specified base-change operation preserves finite colimits after listing finite limits, effective equivalence-relation quotients, descent epimorphisms and distributive coproducts.
reconstruction: An exact/extensive-category or topos comparison is a modern reconstruction; the dual list and its arrows must be interpreted in the intended slice category.
check_reason: The final question is supported. Distributivity over coproducts alone does not prove preservation of all finite colimits.

reconstruction: K91-08 reads uniqueness under T0 where Pro suggests a converse. The mathematical proof gives existence from patch compactness and uniqueness from T0; no converse is assigned to the author.

statement: The questioned notion is a local intersection of constructible subsets, compared with closedness and compactness in the patch topology.
reconstruction: We call this proconstructibility only where the displayed equivalences support it. The uncertain coined word is left unchanged.

statement: Pro reads a warning that the retrocompact pullback hypothesis is too restrictive; K91-08 reads that it is always verified for a scheme morphism.
reconstruction: The latter statement is mathematically correct: pullback of a quasi-compact open immersion is quasi-compact. This is evidence for ink review, not authority to change the transcription.
check_reason: A definite authorial self-criticism cannot be retained when the independent transcription reverses the statement. The note is corrected to a conflict flag.

statement: The upper corollary is cancelled, while lower basis criteria for quasi-compactness and retrocompactness remain live.
reconstruction: The surviving proof uses finite unions of basis opens and quasi-compactness of intersections; it is recorded separately from the cancelled formulation.

statement: The positive constructible-image N.B. in Pro conflicts with the negative K91-08 reading; the following corollary characterizes constructible-image maps by openness in the patch topology.
reconstruction: Spec k(t) → Spec k[t] is a quasi-compact affine map whose image is the nonconstructible generic singleton. This rejects the unqualified positive reading, not a securely established authorial assertion. The alleged les vérifier also conflicts with sont vérifiées.
check_reason: Both note entries depend on unstable readings in the same hypothesis block. Merge as a conflict audit; retain the valid corollary separately in the claims map.

statement: An affine scheme has compact Hausdorff constructible topology; a quasi-separated scheme has locally compact patch topology; a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme has compact patch topology.
reconstruction: Here compact is topological compactness, and the inserted quasi-separated qualification is essential to the stated affine-basis argument.
check_reason: The note accurately preserves the quasi-separated insertion and the absence of a proof of affine compactness on this leaf.

statement: A proconstructible subset of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is the image of a quasi-compact monomorphism.
reconstruction: Construct the absolutely flat envelope and restrict to the closed subset in its patch spectrum; the resulting closed subscheme followed by the envelope map is a monomorphism. This proof is ours, with Olivier as a published counterpart.
check_reason: The strengthened monomorphism assertion is explicit. It is not replaced by the much weaker image of an arbitrary morphism.

statement: Geometric applications are residue-field-compatible maps locally induced on reduced locally closed pieces; constructibility is local on a locally constructible cover and is transitive.
reconstruction: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated domain the patch-open covering argument reduces a covering to finite data. The unresolved X|E subject prevents an unrestricted global assertion for arbitrary E.
check_reason: Keep all three assertions and their quasi-compactness qualification. No general commutation with inverse limits follows.

statement: The page asserts that constructible applications between specified pairs give exactly natural transformations of their Cons functors on affine constructible models.
reconstruction: This is restricted Yoneda for the category generated by the chosen models, conditional on the asserted affine model/refinement properties; the ambiguous ambient category is not silently enlarged.
check_reason: The displayed comparison is genuinely an isomorphism claim. Its missing category definitions are stated as an identification limit.

statement: For affine X=Spec A, the filtered direct limit over finite reduced locally closed affine constructible partitions of the products of section rings yields an absolutely flat envelope with patch spectrum.
reconstruction: The universal pointwise-inverse ring T(A) is an external identification proved in the narrative, not an extra formula supplied by the manuscript. A partition of all of compact patch X by nonempty constructible pieces is necessarily finite.
check_reason: The bottom direct-limit expression and refinement maps fix the direction; keep the initial unsure sign as an ink flag. The published comparison is Olivier, not the w-local cover.

statement: The entire compactness draft on this leaf is cancelled.
reconstruction: Its neighbouring surviving compactness results are on111 and122; sequence in the archive is not proof of chronology.
check_reason: A fully cancelled draft is indexed as withdrawal and is not promoted into another live claim.

statement: The six numbered programme headings culminate in a disputed Néron-spaces line; scan124 is a title sheet.

statement: The diagrams propose adjunctions between schemes, constructible models, compact reduced schemes and flasque ind/pro objects, and write the usual inverse/direct-limit Hom formulas.
reconstruction: The absolutely flat reflection and its opposite scheme adjunction are identified. Claims about the undefined flasque categories remain conditional; exchanging lim and colim without a fixed finite partition is not justified.

statement: A quasi-compact scheme whose underlying Zariski space is Hausdorff is affine; a reduced such scheme is the spectrum of an absolutely flat ring.
reconstruction: The page’s compact means quasi-compact and topologically Hausdorff. It does not assert that every proper scheme is affine.
check_reason: Read the finite affine clopen-cover and disjoint refinement proof; the earlier note’s compact terminology needs this explicit modern explanation.

statement: Four proposed thickness conditions for points of eventually affine inverse systems are compared: eventual fibre genericity, a dense-open pullback condition, constructibility of the point closure, and a constructible open part of it.
reconstruction: Maximal in the fibre is interpreted in the generalization order, i.e. a generic point, not a closed point. Only separately proved implications are accepted; the ML/countability and ambient constructibility ambiguities remain.
check_reason: These entries all audit the same implication diagram. The noetherian insertion and local ideal fragment are retained as distinct subclaims and reading flags; the full equivalence is not asserted.

statement: Valuation-ring points and proper extension of a generic rational map are used to construct a point map between Greenberg objects.
reconstruction: Modern Greenberg functor notation ordinarily includes completeness and chosen unramified lifts. Completeness is not explicit on the retained page. The V-point/K-point comparison must not inherit an accidental bar on X.
check_reason: The point construction is present. Its domain of definition and properness hypotheses are retained, without granting a morphism of schemes from a pointwise map.

statement: Under a dominant generically separable generic-fibre map to a proper target, the page claims existence at a thick point, thickness of its image, a residue-field inclusion and a finite-index promorphism near the closure.
reconstruction: The meaning of finite index and the full thickness hypotheses are not defined on this leaf. The residue-field assertion cannot be strengthened from the stated subfield relation to equality.
check_reason: The small insertions belong to the same Proposition1. They preserve existence and étale qualifications; the proposition is not upgraded to an established modern theorem.

statement: Proposition2 claims constructible images on finitely partitioned X_K-simple pieces with a bounded invariant involving the valuation extension.
reconstruction: Simple, the ell|d invariant, and finite index require recovery before an exact modern theorem can be matched. Greenberg approximation and motivic change-of-variables results are partial comparisons with different hypotheses.
check_reason: The earlier H-G finding is an external candidate, not proof of this exact statement. Merge its audit with the bounded assertion and preserve all missing definitions.

statement: The unit functor A↦A((t))× is the union of affine stages Γ_n recording a Laurent series and its inverse, both bounded below by −n.
reconstruction: The minus sign is required by the equations and by Γ0. Coefficient convolution defines the stages; each equation involves finitely many variables.
check_reason: The stage construction is clear despite the i<−n|i<n ambiguity. Its representability and the scope of the notational caution are treated separately.

statement: The reduced valuation-stratum model Γ′_n→Γ_n is a closed immersion surjective on topological spaces; later stage maps preserve the underlying spaces but change nilpotent structure for strict increases.
reconstruction: The last nonisomorphism statement requires n′>n. At n′=n the map is the identity. This is a proposed ink/inequality correction, not a changed transcription.
check_reason: The theorem’s scheme-theoretic comparison survives; the equality boundary as transcribed is false and flagged.

statement: The dual-number Laurent unit 1+εt^(−1), inverse 1−εt^(−1), lies in Γ1 and not in the zero-valuation power-series copy Γ′1 on dual-number points.
reconstruction: This witnesses nilpotent structure. It does not refute topological surjectivity of Γ′1→Γ1, since a surjective closed immersion need not be surjective on every ring-valued point functor.
check_reason: Retain and rerun the earlier-run example, carefully separating topological surjectivity from functorial surjectivity.

statement: The comparison from pro-morphisms of eventually affine inverse systems to morphisms of their limits is asserted when target stages have finite presentation and source stages are quasi-compact.
reconstruction: A verified modern theorem assumes quasi-compact quasi-separated source stages; the page only inserts quasi-compact. This additional hypothesis is our safe reconstruction, not silently attributed to the manuscript.
check_reason: Merge the proposed Greenberg application with the underlying Hom theorem; a point map alone does not supply stage morphisms or a uniform finite partition.

statement: Polynomial evaluation on a nilpotent ideal with m^(N+1)=0 depends on degree≤N; linear coefficients act on successive graded pieces, and a unit Jacobian gives invertible coordinate change on m^n.
reconstruction: The quotient-algebra and evaluation-set interpretations are kept distinct. Local-ring determinant ∉m is equivalent to unit; det merely nonzero is not.
check_reason: Retain the nilpotence and localness hypotheses and the undecided determinant symbol.

statement: The translation/composition calculation for quadratic coordinate changes has constant, linear and quadratic terms, plus explicit cubic and quartic remainders.
reconstruction: The linear cross coefficient is 2a′2a0a1; dropping remainders is valid for nilpotent evaluation under the stated filtration, or for augmentation-preserving jets, but not for every quotient substitution.
check_reason: The unfinished scan140 calculation and scan142 expansion are one computation, so they are merged and rerun symbolically.

statement: The affine-space rows suggest torsors of lifts under a tangent/derivation module, but the displayed module is not defined here.
reconstruction: For a smooth algebra and a square-zero ideal, differences between two lifts are derivations; that is the precise verified reconstruction. It does not identify every unexplained symbol on the page.

reconstruction: The open subscheme D(det) may be the intended functorial convention, in which case det is required to be a unit. The diagnostic rejects only the literal elementwise interpretation.
check_reason: Rerun the earlier-run test and keep the scheme-open interpretation available.

statement: For A=Q[ε]/(ε³), t↦t+ε fails to preserve (t³), since (t+ε)³=3εt²+3ε²t modulo ε³,t³.

check_reason: Retain and rerun the earlier-run counterexample with every quotient relation checked.
